newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fed's Greenspan gets degree and standing ovation.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Greenspan gets degree and standing ovation.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan got a standing ovation and an honorary degree from Belgium's prestigious Leuven Catholic University on Tuesday for services to world banking and economics.
Greenspan joins eminent figures such as German Chancellor Helmut Kohl who was given an honorary degree last year by the 500-year-old University -- one of the oldest in northern Europe.

Hailed by University Rector Andre Oosterlink as "the most powerful man in the United States...and therefore the world", a less self-possessed man than Greenspan might have been moved to vanity by the praise heaped on him.

Instead the three-term head of the U.S. central bank who has been described by at least one newspaper as being in danger of becoming a myth in his own lifetime, appeared personally moved by the honorary degree and the warm praise.
"This is a real honour for me," he said at the end of his 45-minute speech on central banking and global finance.

In the speech Greenspan praised the success of efforts by the world's leading economies to get inflation down and under control, but warned there could be no relaxation in either the efforts or the vigilance.
"Success must not make us complacent," he said.

He also praised work by the central banks of the group of 10 top industrialised nations to cooperate and coordinate monetary policies, and urged them to encourage the central banks of the rapidly developing Asian and Latin American nations to join in.
"The concept of the domestic market will be even less relevant in a decade than it is today," he said. "Cooperation is the key to success in the future".
